arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Justice O'Connor asked why the Court should interpret the exception broadly.
Justice O'Connor asked if the waiver aimed to cover auto accidents by postal trucks.
Chief Justice Roberts asked if a broken package from a thrown delivery is covered.
Ms. Millett stated that sovereign immunity waiver principles are central to the statute.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The case tests the scope of a federal statute. It waives sovereign immunity for postal negligence. The term negligent transmission defines the limit. Courts must decide if late delivery fits this term.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the scope of federal liability for postal errors. It determines when citizens can sue the government for mail delays. It clarifies the boundary between physical damage and service failures.
